To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) invasive species are a major threat to biodiversity and human well-being, (2) the majority of invasive species are transported by humans, (3) the number of invasive species has increased dramatically in the last 200 years, and (4) invasive species pathways are increasing in number and complexity.

(i) trade is a major pathway for introduction of invasive species; (ii) trade and transport are often coupled; (iii) trade and transport can be used as management tools for invasive species; (iv) the management of trade and transport is a complex task that is not well understood; (v) there is a need for a more integrated approach to the management of trade, transport, and invasive species; (vi) a more holistic understanding of the pathways of invasive species is needed;

understanding and managing the pathways by which non-native species become established in new areas.
understanding how the global movement of people, animals and goods is changing the distribution and abundance of invasive species.
